shapes.text: Ling 285Human Language and TechnologyLecture 3Dynamical Systems 1

Khalil Iskarous
Department of Linguistics
University of Southern California

Dynamical Systems in behavior (Animal)
Dynamical Systems in learning (AI)

Elements: 
8 arms
Ground
Relations between individual arms, ground, and fish are planned by a neural system residing in its head and the rest of its body.
Goal: Keep den

Elements: 
Many parts of tongue
Lips
Velum
larynx
Palate
Pharyngeal Wall
Relations between all these planned by the brain.
Goal: Convey a thought

All of your daily voluntary actions, as well as involuntary actions of your heart, pancreas, neurons, etc…. They’re all dynamical systems
Their elements could be as big as organs or parts theorof downright to cells, and chemicals in them… Biology, Chemistry, and Physics are all about dynamical systems.
So your speech system is a very complex dynamical system. 
Since there are so many dynamical systems, we can use one dynamical system to study another, due to the underlying similarity, despite extreme difference (We’re going up Diotima’s ladder!)

AI is a model of several animal psychological skills:
Knowing
Recognizing
Attending
Acting
Learning

Each word is a vector with thousands of numbers.
We will call them x’s or tokens.
AI knowledge about speech/language whatever is in a few trillion number called weights  or w’s
AI then uses mostly +, - , × , ÷ to combine its knowledge W’s with the vectors you give it
The calculations result in the system predicting a probability distribution function that say: this is my guess for the next word!
How the W’s combine with the X’s is a dynamical system that we will meet later
We will now go to an easier dynamical system: Learning!

Fake it till you make it!
Start out with random, yes totally random, completely random W’s-- any number you want!
We give the system a sequence of words “chickens cackle and ducks ” and ask it to predict the next word by combining its W’s with the input vectors 
Since we know that the next word should be “quack”, we tell it: Change your W’s so that your output pdf looks more like this
Keep exposing the system to more sequences and ask it to predict the next word, billions of times, and keep changing its W’s to improve its guessing.
That’s how LLMs learn and know!
What’s the big deal? Averaging is so easy
SGD starts with a wild guess

What’s the average—the essence—of:
[78, 67, 98, 85, 76, 68, 98, 72]
Pick any random number x as the estimate.
At time 0:
x[0] = 130
Learning rate γ = 25%

Descent = reduce the mistake
The path jitters; its tendency is toward the average.
